name: manual_f37d33
claim: A file showing 'M' in git status/diff with every line changed but zero semantic diff (confirmed via diff with tr -d carriage-return) is EOL-attribute false-dirty, not a real edit - fix once with git add <file> to renormalize, never git checkout-- which can silently discard real changes if you're wrong

decisions.notes: platform/windows/start.ps1 showed as modified with 515 insertions/515 deletions after only touching an unrelated file - .gitattributes marks it eol=crlf but the working tree blob predates that attribute. git add renormalized it cleanly; this matches a prior documented lesson about .cmd files in the same repo.
